Your robot arm just lifted the fridge. With one finger.
You built it last week, for the science fair. Out of an old vacuum cleaner and Dad's drill.
Then you plugged it into your shoulder. And it moved. Like it was yours.
So, what if you built a real cyborg?
At school, everyone wants a high five. You give one. A little too hard.
The arm carries ten backpacks at once. Your friends love it.
And here's something real. Some people already move robot arms with their thoughts, using tiny sensors in the brain.
But that night, the arm moves on its own. It waves at you.
Then your laptop turns on. One message. Upgrade available. Install the other arm?
